books.name: Camping by the Lake
books.focus: went · was · next to · any · than

items.s: Last summer, my family ___ camping by a lake.
items.tip: Last summer = the past: go → went (an irregular past).

no.go: Last summer is the past, so go becomes went.
no.goes: goes is now, for he, she or it; we need the past.
no.going: going needs was or were before it: was going.

items.say: Last summer, my family went camping by a lake.
items.ask: Last summer, my family blank camping by a lake.

items.s: The weather ___ sunny and warm.
items.tip: Past of is = was (one thing); were for more than one.

no.were: were is for more than one (we were); the weather is one thing.
no.be: be needs a helper (will be); in the past it's was.
no.are: are is now; last summer is the past.

items.say: The weather was sunny and warm.
items.ask: The weather blank sunny and warm.

items.s: We put up our tent next ___ the water.
items.tip: next to = beside. It always goes together: next to the lake.

no.of: We say next to, never next of.
no.at: We say next to, never next at.
no.in: We say next to, never next in.

items.say: We put up our tent next to the water.
items.ask: We put up our tent next blank the water.

items.s: We didn't have ___ chairs, so we sat on logs.
items.tip: any after not: We didn't have any chairs. (some is for yes-sentences.)

no.some: some is for yes-sentences; after didn't we use any.
no.a: a is for one thing; chairs means more than one.
no.much: much is for things we can't count (much water); we can count chairs.

items.say: We didn't have any chairs, so we sat on logs.
items.ask: We didn't have blank chairs, so we sat on logs.

items.s: We were tired ___ we swam all afternoon.
items.tip: because gives the reason: tired because we swam.

no.what: what asks about or names a thing; it can't give a reason.
no.or: or gives a choice (tea or milk), not a reason.

items.say: We were tired because we swam all afternoon.
items.ask: We were tired blank we swam all afternoon.

items.s: My sister asked, “___ you see the stars last night?”
items.tip: Past questions start with Did + verb: Did you see…?

no.Was: Was you see isn't English; past questions with a doing word use Did.
no.Are: Are is for now, and are doesn't go with see.
no.Has: Has is for he, she or it, and last night needs Did.

items.say: My sister asked, “Did you see the stars last night?”
items.ask: My sister asked, “blank you see the stars last night?”

items.s: The lake was colder ___ the swimming pool at home.
items.tip: colder than: -er words compare two things with than (not then).

no.then: then means 'next' or 'after that'; to compare we use than.
no.that: that points to something; after colder we need than.
no.as: as goes with as … as (as cold as); after colder use than.

items.say: The lake was colder than the swimming pool at home.
items.ask: The lake was colder blank the swimming pool at home.

items.s: We are ___ to go back next year!
items.tip: be going to + verb = a plan for the future.

no.go: are go isn't English; we say are going to.
no.went: went is the past; next year is the future.
no.gone: are gone to go isn't English; we say are going to.

items.say: We are going to go back next year!
items.ask: We are blank to go back next year!

items.s: My grandma's birthday is ___ Sunday.
items.tip: on + days: on Sunday, on my birthday.

no.in: in is for months and years (in May); days take on.
no.at: at is for clock times (at three o'clock); days take on.
no.to: to shows moving to a place, not a day.

items.say: My grandma's birthday is on Sunday.
items.ask: My grandma's birthday is blank Sunday.

items.s: We are making a big cake ___ her.
items.tip: for = to give to someone: a cake for her, a present for you.

no.to: We make a cake for someone; to is for giving: give it to her.
no.at: at is for places and times, not for the person who gets it.
no.of: of shows belonging (a slice of cake).

items.say: We are making a big cake for her.
items.ask: We are making a big cake blank her.

items.s: Oh no! There isn't ___ sugar in the cupboard!
items.tip: isn't any = none at all. any goes with not.

no.some: some is for yes-sentences; after isn't we use any.
no.many: many is for things we can count; we can't count sugar.
no.a: a is for one thing we can count; we don't say a sugar.

items.say: Oh no! There isn't any sugar in the cupboard!
items.ask: Oh no! There isn't blank sugar in the cupboard!

items.s: Mum goes to the shop ___ buys a big bag.
items.tip: and joins two things Mum does: goes and buys.

no.but: but shows something different; going and buying go together, so and.
no.of: of shows belonging; it can't join two actions.
no.the: the goes before a thing, not before buys.

items.say: Mum goes to the shop and buys a big bag.
items.ask: Mum goes to the shop blank buys a big bag.

items.s: “We ___ be very quiet. It's a surprise!”
items.tip: must + verb = it's very important: We must be quiet.

no.has: has be isn't English, and has is for he, she or it.
no.are: are be isn't English; one 'be' word is enough.

items.say: “We must be very quiet. It's a surprise!”
items.ask: “We blank be very quiet. It's a surprise!”

items.s: Grandma arrives ___ four o'clock.
items.tip: at + a clock time: at four o'clock.

no.in: in is for months and parts of the day (in the morning).
no.on: on is for days and dates (on Sunday).
no.to: to shows going to a place, not a time.

items.say: Grandma arrives at four o'clock.
items.ask: Grandma arrives blank four o'clock.

items.s: She opens the door and sees ___ her family.
items.tip: all her family = every person in her family.

no.every: every goes straight before a thing (every day), not before her.
no.any: any is for questions and not-sentences.
no.many: many her family isn't English; we'd say many of.

items.say: She opens the door and sees all her family.
items.ask: She opens the door and sees blank her family.

items.s: “This is ___ best birthday ever!” she says.
items.tip: the + best: the best birthday, the biggest cake.

no.a: best means the top one, so it takes the, not a.
no.an: an goes before a vowel sound, and best needs the.
no.most: best already means 'most good'; most best isn't English.

items.say: “This is the best birthday ever!” she says.
items.ask: “This is blank best birthday ever!” she says.

books.name: The School Pet
books.focus: called · than · every · for · going to

items.s: Our class has a pet tortoise ___ Shelly.
items.tip: called = with the name: a tortoise called Shelly.

no.call: a tortoise call Shelly? We need called (it has the name).
no.calls: calls is something she does now; we need called.
no.calling: calling means shouting or phoning, not her name.

items.say: Our class has a pet tortoise called Shelly.
items.ask: Our class has a pet tortoise blank Shelly.

items.s: She is ten years old, so she is older ___ us!
items.tip: older than: compare two things with than.

no.then: then means 'after that'; to compare we use than.
no.as: as goes with as … as (as old as us).
no.that: that points to something; after older we need than.

items.say: She is ten years old, so she is older than us!
items.ask: She is ten years old, so she is older blank us!

items.s: Shelly eats lettuce ___ day.
items.tip: every day = Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday… all the days.

no.much: much is for amounts (much lettuce), not for days.
no.many: many goes with more than one: many days, not many day.
no.lots: lots of goes before things (lots of lettuce), not before day.

items.say: Shelly eats lettuce every day.
items.ask: Shelly eats lettuce blank day.

items.s: Last week, nobody could find ___!
items.tip: After find we say her, not she: find her.

no.she: she goes before a doing word; after find we say her.
no.they: they is more than one, and after find we'd say them.

items.say: Last week, nobody could find her!
items.ask: Last week, nobody could find blank!

items.s: We looked ___ her everywhere.
items.tip: look for = try to find: We looked for her.

no.at: look at means just look with your eyes; to find her we look for her.
no.to: look to her doesn't mean trying to find her.
no.on: look on her isn't what we mean; look for = try to find.

items.say: We looked for her everywhere.
items.ask: We looked blank her everywhere.

items.s: In the end, Tom found her asleep ___ his school bag!
items.tip: in = inside something: in his bag.

no.at: at is for a place we visit (at school), not inside a bag.
no.of: of shows belonging, not a place.
no.to: to shows moving towards a place.

items.say: In the end, Tom found her asleep in his school bag!
items.ask: In the end, Tom found her asleep blank his school bag!

items.s: Tom was very surprised, ___ everyone laughed.
items.tip: and joins two things that happened.

no.or: or gives a choice; both things really happened, so and.
no.of: of shows belonging; it can't join two ideas.

items.say: Tom was very surprised, and everyone laughed.
items.ask: Tom was very surprised, blank everyone laughed.

items.s: Next week, we are ___ to build her a new house.
items.tip: be going to + verb = a plan: We are going to build…

no.go: are go isn't English; we say are going to.
no.went: went is the past; next week is the future.
no.goes: goes is for he, she or it now; after are we need going.

items.say: Next week, we are going to build her a new house.
items.ask: Next week, we are blank to build her a new house.
